note: Set A correctly reads the stacked-bar totals (45/40/35/30/25/20/15/10 mm across the span positions) and gives plausible per-layer values for glass_biax and medium_density_foam, keeping web0/web1 and span position as conditions. Set B repeatedly binds the total stack height to a single thin layer (glass_biax 45/42/38/32/12 mm, CarbonUD 13/23 mm), which is plainly wrong given the 0–60 mm axis and the layer legend, and it also contradicts itself (glass_biax 42 mm vs 4 mm at FFA-W3-360 25% for both webs; 12 mm vs 3 mm at FFA-W3-211 100%). B additionally emits trivial zero-thickness claims for the empty circular 0%/2% positions and its quotes are bare token lists that do not support any numeric value. A is clearly the more faithful set despite a few uncertain layer readings.
remarks: Both sets build quotes by stitching non-contiguous text-layer fragments ('...'), so no quote is a literal passage; B's quotes ('web0, FFA-W3-360 25%, glass_biax') never contain the axis or any number and cannot support the values. The web0 and web1 panels look nearly identical, yet A gives different medium_density_foam values for the two webs at the same span position (13 vs 10 mm at 77%, 27 vs 25 mm at 44%) — at least one of each pair is likely a misread, but the bars are too small to resolve. Neither set extracts the thin layers (CarbonUD, Gelcoat, glass_triax, glass_uni) or states that the circular 0%/2% positions have no web/layup, and neither records the figure caption as context for the 'thickness' attribute, which A leaves otherwise unnamed.
